title: Remove the stray tracked root files True and unspecified
lead: The repository root tracks two files, `True` and `unspecified`, that commit 5716ab7 ("s367 done") added. They look like the output of a shell redirect gone wrong and belong to no feature.
findings_note: s415 review 2026-10-30, later note: the repository root tracks files named True and unspecified, added by 5716ab7 (s367 done)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** finding which command wrote them, beyond a test that stops it happening again if it was slicer.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Stray tracked files at the root confuse readers and tools, and they may mean a command wrote to a path built from a Python value (`True`) or a placeholder (`unspecified`).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `True` and `unspecified` at the repository root: remove them with `git rm`.
- If `git log -p 5716ab7 -- True unspecified` shows slicer wrote them (a path built from a value), the module that did it and a regression test.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - None if the files came from a hand-run shell redirect. If slicer wrote them, a test that the command no longer writes a file named after a value.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Look at 5716ab7's diff for the two files to see what wrote them.
2. `git rm` both files.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `git ls-files True unspecified` prints nothing. `slicer check` passes, and the full suite stays green.
